\section[a etapa]{a etapa — the stage, the step}

\label{lesson:PT-C273-etapa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the period, then the Portuguese for immediately.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a etapa}
\textbf{a etapa} — \textquotedblleft{}the stage, the step\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A primeira etapa da viagem foi de comboio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The first stage of the journey was by train.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Por etapas} — in stages, step by step.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{etapa} was borrowed from French \emph{étape}, once a stopping place on a march, which EtymDB traces to a Germanic word \emph{stapel} \textquotedblleft{}a post, a depot\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a etapa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a etapa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a etapa}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the period, then the Portuguese for immediately, then say \emph{a etapa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a etapa mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The stage, the step\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[a fase]{a fase — the phase}

\label{lesson:PT-C273-fase}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for immediately, then the Portuguese for the stage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a fase}
\textbf{a fase} — \textquotedblleft{}the phase\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O meu filho está numa fase difícil.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My son is going through a difficult phase.}
\end{quote}

\emph{As fases da lua} — the phases of the moon.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fase} comes from Greek \emph{phásis} \textquotedblleft{}an appearance\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), first said of the moon as it shows a different face.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a sequência]{a sequência — the sequence, the series}

\label{lesson:PT-C273-sequencia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the stage, then the Portuguese for the phase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a sequência}
\textbf{a sequência} — \textquotedblleft{}the sequence, the series\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O filme tem uma sequência muito bonita no mar.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The film has a very beautiful sequence at sea.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Em sequência} — one after the other.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sequência} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{sequentia} \textquotedblleft{}a following, a series\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{sequī} \textquotedblleft{}to follow\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a sucessão]{a sucessão — the succession, a string (of events)}

\label{lesson:PT-C273-sucessao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the phase, then the Portuguese for the sequence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a sucessão}
\textbf{a sucessão} — \textquotedblleft{}the succession, a string (of events)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Foi uma sucessão de erros.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It was a string of mistakes.}
\end{quote}

Also who comes next on a throne or at the head of a firm.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sucessão} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{successiō} \textquotedblleft{}a coming after, a following on\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{succēdere} \textquotedblleft{}to come after\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a cronologia]{a cronologia — the chronology, the order of events}

\label{lesson:PT-C273-cronologia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the sequence, then the Portuguese for the succession.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a cronologia}
\textbf{a cronologia} — \textquotedblleft{}the chronology, the order of events\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O professor escreveu a cronologia no quadro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The teacher wrote the chronology on the board.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Por ordem cronológica} — in order of time.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{cronologia} is a learned word built from Greek \emph{khrónos} \textquotedblleft{}time\textquotedblright{} and \emph{-logía} \textquotedblleft{}an account, a reckoning\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB traces \emph{crónica} to the same \emph{khrónos}).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
